findings.text: Compat system call entry starts with hardware interrupts already disabled, exchanges the GS base, preserves the user stack pointer aside, switches to kernel page tables and kernel stack, then builds a register save area containing user segment selectors, stack pointer, flags, instruction pointer and truncated call number before invoking the 32-bit fast dispatcher. On return it selects between an opportunistic register restore return and a full restore path, with virtualized guests forced to the full path.
A small compatibility entry clears branch history state and transfers control unconditionally to the C routine that emulates the legacy vector.

User originated FRED entry uses a common prologue, calls the C dispatcher for user events, then runs a common epilogue and returns with the user return instruction, with an exception table entry covering the return.
Kernel originated FRED entry uses the same prologue, calls the C dispatcher for kernel events, then runs the epilogue and returns with the kernel return instruction.

The virtualization helper builds a synthetic event frame on the current task stack without a privilege stack switch, emulates required red zone reservation and alignment, preserves the frame pointer, fabricates zero event data and error code with a caller supplied stack segment, then saves registers and calls the C handler for virtualized interrupts before exiting.

The synthetic frame described for virtualized entry is eight eight-byte slots ordered from low to high as error code, return address, code segment plus auxiliary info, flags, stack pointer, stack segment plus event info, event data and a reserved zero slot, totaling sixty four bytes.
FRED other event subcodes use value one for the 64-bit system call mechanism and value two for the 32-bit fast system call mechanism.

Other event dispatch checks the event vector and mode indicator: long mode plus the 64-bit subcode records the call number and invokes 64-bit dispatch, non long mode plus the 32-bit subcode with compat enabled invokes 32-bit fast dispatch, otherwise it raises an invalid opcode fault. Both dispatch paths preset the result to not implemented before the call.

Software interrupt dispatch routes the breakpoint trap number to breakpoint handling and the overflow trap number to overflow handling, routes the legacy vector to compat emulation only when compat is enabled, and otherwise rewinds the saved instruction pointer by the recorded length, sets the resume flag, clears the software event marker and raises a protection fault with a code derived from the vector.

Invalid or fatal FRED events are classified by saved stack level: nonzero level logs at emergency severity and halts via fatal exception handling, while level zero opens a fault reporting region, logs at alert severity, attempts controlled reporting and may suppress the kill signal if reporting succeeds, always bracketed by no instrument entry and exit.

The 32-bit fast return predicate first forces the saved instruction pointer to a landing address inside the compat virtual system call page, runs the inner fast handler, then permits the fast user return only when not virtualized, when instruction pointer still matches the landing address, when code and stack selectors match expected user values, and when resume trap and virtual mode flags are all clear.

The inner 32-bit fast handler records the call number, randomizes the kernel stack protector, enables instrumentation and interrupts, loads the saved base pointer from the user stack slot addressed by the low half of the user stack pointer, and on access failure sets a fault result, disables interrupts, ends instrumentation, exits to user mode and requests the slow return path.

The inner 32-bit fast path runs with interrupts enabled across user memory access and dispatch work, and explicitly disables them again before instrumentation close and exit when the user stack read fails.
32-bit entry marks the current thread as compat when that configuration exists and derives the call number from the low 32 bits of the saved original accumulator interpreted as signed.

32-bit dispatch with interrupts on only calls into the compat table when the number is below the compat count, applying a speculation safe index clamp, and the table implementation falls back to a not implemented handler for unlisted numbers.

64-bit dispatch runs entry work that may randomize stack and adjust the number, then tries the 64-bit table and on miss tries the extended table, closes instrumentation, performs exit work, and only then allows the fast return when not virtualized, when saved counter and flag shadows match, when selectors match expected user values, when the instruction pointer is below the maximum user address, and when resume and trap flags are clear.

Each 64-bit family helper bounds checks its number, clamps the index against speculation, stores the handler result into the saved accumulator and reports hit or miss; the extended family subtracts its base bit first, honors its configuration gate, and returns not implemented when disabled or out of range.

System vector handlers live in a fixed array indexed by vector minus the first system vector, populated initially with handlers for error, spurious, timer, platform messaging, scheduling, call function, reboot, threshold, deferred error, thermal, work and virtualization notifications, installable only for system vectors before setup completes and only into empty slots.

Completion marks all vectors below the first external vector as used, marks each populated system vector as used, replaces every empty system slot with a spurious handler, then latches setup done to forbid later installs.

External interrupt dispatch rejects vectors below the first external vector, routes system vectors through the system table under entry tracking and instrumentation with a speculation safe index, and routes ordinary device vectors through the common interrupt path.

Hardware exception dispatch optimizes the page fault vector first, then maps divide, debug, bound, invalid opcode, device unavailable, double fault, task state, segment, stack, protection, coprocessor, alignment and SIMD vectors to their respective handlers, with machine check, virtualization, protection and secure guest vectors included only under their configurations, defaulting to invalid event handling.
Synchronous software exception dispatch handles only the breakpoint and overflow vectors, sending any other vector to invalid event handling.

User event entry saves the error code from the original accumulator slot, invalidates that slot so number queries fail safe, then dispatches by event type to external, nonmaskable, hardware, software interrupt, privileged debug and synchronous software paths plus the other event system call path, falling through to invalid handling on mismatch.

Kernel event entry performs the same error code save and slot invalidation as user entry but omits the other event system call type, dispatching only external, nonmaskable, hardware, privileged debug and synchronous software types before invalid handling.
The C handler for virtualized entry accepts only external and nonmaskable event types, delegating each to its FRED handler and warning once on any other type.

One macro family emits external declarations for 32-bit handlers with a common prefix and a nonreturn variant, a second use emits table initializers from the generated list, and a third use emits dispatch cases returning handler results, with the compat selector choosing between compat and native symbols.
Compat emulation defaults on unless the default disabled configuration is set, is stored read only after init, and can be overridden early by parsing a boolean command line argument.

Vector 128 is treated as externally injected when its bit is set in the local interrupt controller in service register, except on paravirtual guests where the controller is emulated and the check always reports not external; guest mode validity depends on full virtual controller control by the secure module.

Compat entry and return apply speculation and leak controls including branch history clearing, indirect branch barriers, return training mitigation, buffer clearing, stack erasure before fast return, and zeroing of caller visible scratch registers that are not already known to user code.

The fast 32-bit return delays the switch back to user page tables until after the final reference to kernel stack memory, uses only registers safe to clobber for that switch, restores callee preserved user registers from the save area, and skips restoring registers that user code already knows or that trampoline code will fix.

Compat entry constructs its save area by pushing user stack segment, user stack pointer, flags, compat code segment, return address, truncated call number and then the general registers with selected registers preset, establishing the in memory order expected by the return path.

Virtualized FRED exit selects at boot between restoring the saved frame pointer with no operations and discarding the register save area then issuing the kernel event return that can clear nonmaskable state.
Several handlers are marked visible for assembly or cross file linkage, including the fast 32-bit dispatcher, the 64-bit dispatcher and both FRED C entries, plus the 32-bit call table.
